item.title: CKB Talk Daily Brief - 2026-11-03
item.description: ## 今日发生了什么 过去 24 小时的帖子主要围绕资助收尾、提案补充和开发工具发布展开 [S01, S09, S16]。iCKB 宣布资助结项并完成 CCC 迁移，Cellula on Fiber 在被质疑后补充发布 npm 包，Kaze Unitour 确认收到首场款项 [S01, S18, S09, S14]。技术侧有 CKB Cell Framework 发布和 Rust/TypeScript 锁脚本性能对比，社区也继续讨论 Tranfr 的恢复方案 [S16, S17, S04]。 ## 重点话题 iCKB 的资助已结项且款项全部花完，但项目继续运行 [S01]；同一作者还宣布 ickb.org 新 DApp、SDK 和 bot 全部切换到 CCC，替代 Lumos 版本 [S18]；此外作者表示因近期 LLM 事件重新检查了 iCKB 合约安全 [S19]。 Cellula on Fiber 提案称要给 Fiber 补上普通用户钱包、商户两行代码结账和 AI agent 支付入口 [S06]；有成员指出 npm 上 cellula-mcp 说明写着 agent 尚未发布、公开仓库也没有 pay-with-fiber [S07]；项目方随后称 cellula-agent 0.1.0 与 cellula-mcp 0.4.1 已上 npm 并更新提案 [S09]；也有人表达支持 [S08, S10]。 Kaze X CKB Unitour 方面，Machakos 大学 GDGoC 负责人确认 11 月 18—21 日可能举办，但仍待委员会成员私下支持后正式确认...

item.title: Tranfr — Programmable Recovery for CKB (3 posts)
item.description: This is indeed a missing part of the original cheque lock design, and I think it would be possible to add support for additional transfer methods using a fork lock from cheque. item.title: [DIS] Cellula on Fiber: a wallet, a checkout and an AI agent on a public mainnet LSP (5 posts)
item.description: Fiber works. What it lacks is a way in for people who will never run a node, and Fiber Link, funded by this DAO, says the same. Cellula gives it three: a wallet people open with their face or fingerprint, a checkout any shop adds with two lines, and an agent that lets AI pay for what it uses within limits a person sets. All three pay in seconds over Fiber, and all three already run on testnet. This proposal takes them to mainnet, on a public LSP (the node that opens payment channels for wallets, so they never need one of their own) that any Fiber wallet or app can use. LusoCryptoLabs asks for $22,258.48 (and up to $1,664 of contingency, paid only if used), in CKB over five payments, each...

item.title: [DIS] CrowdCell: From Testnet Demo to a Crowdfunding Product on CKB | CrowdCell：把 CKB 测试网上的免信任众筹做成产品 (1 posts)
item.description: Good question, and agreed, once real money moves someone has to pay for keeping it running. The plan is in §6.4: a fee paid by the creator on funded campaigns only, enforced on-chain, nothing on failed ones, so the same shape as yours. It’s left out of this grant on purpose because it only makes sense on mainnet after the audit. The first proposal had 5%, which RetricSu pushed for as start higher and lower it later, but 1-2% like VeriCell is a fair point and I’ll look at it again for the mainnet proposal. The part I’m less sure about is who gets it, a treasury multisig or whoever runs the hosted site. And with CSR in the picture, part of it could go to whoever settles the campaign.

item.title: Introducing CKB Cell Framework: typed Cells and declarative validation in Rust (1 posts)
item.description: Hi everyone, We’d like to introduce CKB Cell Framework, a Rust framework for building CKB contracts, developed by FoundationLab. Our goal is to make CKB contracts easier to write, understand, and test. The framework brings together typed Cell loading, declarative constraints, automatic serialization, transaction construction, and local VM testing. The main building blocks are: CellCodec generates encoding, strict decoding, and wire-format schemas for application data. Cells declares the inputs, outputs, and dependencies an operation needs, with constraints for scripts, capacity, positions, and data. Context<C> gives handlers access to the loaded Cell collection and executing Script....

item.title: Same lock script in Rust and in ckb-js-vm: 15k cycles vs 15M (1 posts)
item.description: I wrote the same CKB lock script twice, once in Rust and once in TypeScript for ckb-js-vm, and ran both through the same 58 scenarios in the real CKB-VM. They agree on every accept/reject decision. The cost is very different, and most of the difference is not where I expected. The script is the session lock from ckb-session-kit. It lets a browser-held session key spend a bounded amount (per-transaction limit, optional single recipient, optional rate limit, no splitting of session cells, no type scripts the key could use to freeze funds), while the owner can always sweep. It also has a token mode that bounds xUDT amounts the same way. It delegates signature checks to the standard locks, so...

item.title: CKBdapps 2.0：为 CKB 生态重新搭建的项目目录 (2 posts)
item.description: 这次改版帅多了。great work！ 等以后收录的项目越来越多，会不会考虑在现有的「相似项目」之外，加入一些更智能的 matching 建议？ 比如不只是推荐同类项目，还能根据技术栈、依赖关系和实际需求，发现哪些项目之间有潜在的集成机会、哪些组件可以复用，甚至哪些开发者值得互相认识、合作。 之前我们脑暴过一个 Project Matchmaker 的想法。感觉 CKBdapps 已经有了很好的结构化项目目录，未来或许可以成为这类生态协作推荐的自然入口。 ArthurZhang: 比如不只是推荐同类项目，还能根据技术栈、依赖关系和实际需求，发现哪些项目之间有潜在的集成机会、哪些组件可以复用，甚至哪些开发者值得互相认识、合作。 我觉得完全没有问题——只要项目的ReadMe里描述清楚相关内容，再把规则定下来，让AI跑一遍，就可以生成项目与项目之间的关联性关系。

item.title: Myelin Is in Production — Where Could It Take Us Next? (2 posts)
item.description: For anyone new to the project, Myelin is an off-chain runtime I’m building around CKB’s Cell model. It handles application state changes and keeps a history that can be replayed and checked. A session might cover a match, a dungeon run or a stretch of activity in a persistent world. I started it to explore how applications could make use of CKB’s approach to state and verification without sending every interaction to the blockchain. Myelin is now running in production behind games on UTXOPlay. I’m rather pleased to finally be able to write that.
